pages.title: Wood to a working workshop
pages.intro: Turn logs into fuel, planks and working stations before investing in powered production. The server's Woodworking page follows its live configuration.

steps.label: Split your fuel
steps.text: Make a chopping block from a placed log and an axe. Place wood on it with right-click, then hold right-click with an axe to chop. Keep fuel separate from logs reserved for boards; do not assume a fixed firewood yield.

steps.label: Build a matched pair
steps.text: At each trestle position, right-click a stick, another stick, then rope. Build the second directly beside the first, not diagonally. Lay a log across the pair. The pack disables the alternative grid-crafted sawhorse: use this in-world assembly.

steps.label: Saw boards or beams
steps.text: Stand at an end and hold right-click with a saw. Use tool mode to choose planks or support beams. A normal saw is allowed in this pack; a pitsaw is another option. Keep matching logs in your inventory for continuous feeding. Stripping bark from the side is a separate operation: a log cannot be both sawn and stripped.

steps.label: Spend boards on capability
steps.text: Build a Toolsmith workbench for assembly and a grindstone for maintenance. Their native recipes use planks; the workbench also needs a saw, while the grindstone needs an appropriate rock. Continue into the existing Toolsmith guides rather than replacing its handles, grips, bindings or treatments with ordinary grid tools.

steps.label: Automate after the hand route works
steps.text: A sawmill needs its frame, carriage, sash, crankshaft, feed levers and blade kit, plus an axle driven by mechanical power. Use its native page for assembly and feeding. Do not craft a bare frame and expect it to cut.

pages.title: Ore to useful metal equipment
pages.intro: Keep ore preparation, smelting, shaping and assembly as separate jobs. The first useful metal tools unlock more workstations; later metals do not all follow the copper route.

steps.label: Find and prepare ore
steps.text: Use prospecting to locate deposits, then bring back ore chunks. ImmersiveOreCrush adds in-world crushing by striking chunks on the ground. Start with a hammer and check the interaction prompt. Do not treat every mineral as interchangeable: keep smelting ore separate from quartz, borax and pigments for the materials workshop.

steps.label: Make the first usable metal
steps.text: Prepare charcoal and fired clay equipment. Follow Smelting for crucible charges, fuel and casting. Make copper ingots or castable heads as appropriate; follow the live alloy recipe when moving to bronze. Do not put iron ore through a copper casting workflow.

steps.label: Shape a head, then assemble
steps.text: Use Smithing for anvil work and Toolsmith's crafting-method guide for the matching modular assembly. Prioritize mining and sawing capability to expand the workshop. The Toolsmith workbench, component choices and maintenance remain part of this route; a head alone is not your finished tool.

steps.label: Cool, maintain, then progress
steps.text: Manual Quenching adds cooling hot metal without dropping it; consult Quenching for the actual mechanic, not an assumed universal stat bonus. Repair and maintain tools using Toolsmith's own instructions. Move through the native iron and steel progression only when you have the required fuel, furnace and forging setup; use Reforging when recovering Toolsmith metal parts.

pages.title: Powders to glazed working ceramics
pages.intro: Start with one clear glaze and one color. This is a materials-processing chain, not a list of decorative variants: powdered minerals become frit, glaze and a usable fired bowl.

steps.label: Set up the powder bench
steps.text: Prepare a pulverizer, quern, barrels, water and high-temperature fuel. The native guide describes crushing minerals and then grinding them into powders. Reserve powdered quartz for glaze base and frit; keep coloring powders separate from metal intended for smelting.

steps.label: Mix a clear base
steps.text: In a barrel, combine water with supported clay to make clay slurry. Add powdered quartz to slurry for clear glaze base. Follow the barrel recipe for quantities; milky base is a different branch using powdered cassiterite.

steps.label: Bake and grind a blue frit
steps.text: For the copper-based blue option, mix lime, powdered copper, powdered quartz and powdered borax using the shown grid recipe. Heat the frit mix into baked frit, then grind it into ground frit. Ground pigment is not yet finished glaze.

steps.label: Rest, coat, and fire again
steps.text: Combine clear base and ground blue frit in a barrel and seal it for 48 hours. Coat a fired bowl using the glazing-bowls barrel recipe, then fire the raw glazed result. The finished glazed bowl is a meal and liquid container; stop here before branching into stamps, tiles or colored glass.

pages.title: Storage that supports the work
pages.intro: Store materials at the station that consumes them. Choose containers for access and accepted contents, not just appearance.

steps.label: Keep working stock visible
steps.text: Stack fuel and boards near the woodworking and metal stations, leaving room to use the machines. Ground storage is the first option, not a substitute for every container. Check the native placement controls before building a wall of inaccessible stock.

steps.label: Give bulk inputs a resource bin
steps.text: Craft a Purposeful Storage resource bin from planks. Its shipped restrictions include ore chunks, nuggets and metal bits, charcoal, quartz, sticks and selected powders. Keep separate bins by workflow; it is not an unrestricted chest. Check held descriptions for accepted groups before moving all your stock.

steps.label: Separate pantry from workshop
steps.text: Containers Bundle's food cupboard is a functional food-storage branch made from boards and metal nails-and-strips. Its block definition gives vegetable and grain spoilage modifiers; it does not promise the same benefit for every food. Keep pantry storage separate from ore and powders, and still use proper preservation conditions.

steps.label: Carry and sort deliberately
steps.text: Carry On is enabled: check its key bindings and container interaction before relocating a loaded store. Sortable Storage adds a sort button to storage containers; use it to tidy a store, not as a promise of automatic routing between stations. Keep input and output stock separate.
